# Azurearm

**Parity grade: B** · SDK `hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm@v4.81.0` · last audited 2026-09-12 (`f973f0c90`)

### Known gaps

- Storage RP account state (StorageProvider.accounts) does not survive a snapshot/restore cycle -- only InMemoryBackend's resource-group/generic-resource/provider-registration state is persisted (see ops.StorageAccountCRUD). Fix is additive: give StorageProvider its own Snapshot/Restore and wire it into Handler.Snapshot/Restore alongside the backend's.
- ServiceBus RP state (ServiceBusProvider's namespaces/queues/topics/subscriptions maps) does not survive a snapshot/restore cycle either, the same known gap as StorageAccountCRUD above and for the same reason -- no ResourceProvider's own state is currently wired into Handler.Snapshot/Restore.
- TestTerraform_Azure_ServiceBus (M9) could not be confirmed against a live tofu apply on this milestone's local macOS development sandbox, due to the same pre-existing host-OS-specific TLS-trust gap documented for M7/M8 (AZURE.md section 10.10) -- apply fails at ARM's own metadata-discovery call, before reaching any ServiceBus-specific code. Compensating verification: test/integration/azurearm_test.go's TestIntegration_AzureARM_ServiceBusLifecycleAndCrossServiceWiring exercises the identical ARM CRUD + cross-service-wiring path over plain HTTP and passed; wire-shape questions were answered by reading the pinned terraform-provider-azurerm/go-azure-sdk source directly. Should be re-confirmed against a green CI run (expected to work on Linux).
- Token endpoint accepts any (or a missing) client_id/grant_type without validation and always issues a token; a malformed client_credentials request should arguably 400 with invalid_request/unsupported_grant_type per RFC 6749, matching AAD's own error shape more closely.
- Direct-data-plane storage resources (azurerm_storage_container/_blob/_queue/_table) are covered as of M8 via the new services/azurestoragevhost virtual-hosted-style listener (AZURE.md section 10.8 finding (9)); azurerm_storage_share (File Share) remains out of scope -- no gopherstack file-share service exists.
- Multi-account namespace isolation: all ARM-created storage accounts alias one shared Blob/Queue/Table container/queue/table namespace (services/azureblob/azurequeue/azuretable discard the account-name path segment entirely). Two ARM storage accounts see each other's containers. Deferred to M10 per AZURE.md section 10.4's original note; StorageAccounts.RegisterAccount/DeleteAccount (interfaces.go) is the forward-compat seam for that fix.
- ARM error codes are a small hand-picked table (errors.go's errorDetails), not audited against ARM's full published error-code catalog the way services/sqs's errorDetails table has been over multiple audit passes.
- management locks, Azure Policy, RBAC/Microsoft.Authorization, ARM template deployments (Microsoft.Resources/deployments), PATCH-merge semantics beyond full-replace, $filter/$expand and nextLink pagination on list operations, cross-subscription/cross-tenant, resource moves, What-If, and LRO polling are all explicitly out of MVP scope per AZURE.md section 10.1/10.3 -- not bugs, deliberate scope boundaries for this milestone.
- Flexible servers: only the listed operations are modelled. PostgreSQL administrators (Entra), backups, migrations, virtual-network subnet usage, private DNS zone suffix, and MySQL updateConfigurations (batch), maintenances, logFiles, backupAndExport, advanced threat protection, Entra administrators, failover, detachVNet, resetGtid and private endpoint connections answer from the generic store or 404.
- Flexible servers: replicas and point-in-time/geo restores are state-level (a copy of the source configuration and database list); under the docker engine they are refused with 400 InvalidParameterValue because a new container would start without the source data or the administrator password. Replication is not run.
- Flexible servers: server parameter changes are stored, validated against a documented subset of parameters and flagged pending-restart, but are not applied to the docker engine; the MySQL max_connections default is the engine default (151) rather than the memory-derived Azure default; PostgreSQL max_connections follows the documented per-SKU table.
- Flexible servers: firewall rules (including the 0.0.0.0 allow-Azure-services rule) are stored and validated but not enforced - the docker engine listens on loopback only; engines are not relaunched after a gopherstack restart or snapshot restore; the 7-day automatic restart of a stopped server, maintenance windows, HA failover, data encryption and Entra authentication are stored but not acted on.
- Flexible servers: no Terraform azurerm fixture (azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server, azurerm_mysql_flexible_server) yet; the SDK-driven tests are the only wire proof.
- AKS: runCommand answers 501 NotImplemented (no pods are scheduled to run commands in); abort, rotateClusterCertificates, resetAADProfile, resetServicePrincipalProfile, maintenanceConfigurations, trustedAccessRoleBindings, snapshots, machines, managedNamespaces and private endpoint connections are not modelled (the generic store keeps what is PUT).
- AKS: node pools are metadata; no VMs back them and the k3s engine runs one server node regardless of pool counts. stop removes the container, so k3s state is lost across stop/start and across restore.
- AKS: addon profiles, AAD, auto-upgrade, http proxy, security and storage profiles are stored and returned but not interpreted; the VM catalog and Kubernetes patch versions are representative subsets; the kubeconfig carries a bearer token only (no client certificates).
- Container Apps: init containers, subPath mounts, NfsAzureFile volumes, additional TCP ports, exposedPort/TCP transport routing, session affinity, CORS, ipSecurityRestrictions enforcement, custom domains, Dapr runtime, probes and managed-identity registry pulls are stored but not run or enforced.
- Container Apps: KEDA scale rules other than the http/tcp concurrency settings (queue, custom) are stored but never scale replicas; scale-out is driven by in-flight requests through the ingress.
- Container Apps jobs: Schedule and Event triggers are stored and validated but never fire (only start runs an execution); replicaRetryLimit and replicaTimeout are not enforced.
- Container Apps: restored revisions have no replicas until their first request (or a restart), even with minReplicas above 0.
- Container Apps: getAuthtoken, listCustomHostNameAnalysis, diagnostics, authConfigs, daprComponents, certificates, sourcecontrols, javaComponents and sessionPools are not modelled (the generic store keeps what is PUT); the operation status URL is locations/{loc}/operations/{id} rather than the service's containerappOperationStatuses path.
- Container Instances: interactive exec and attach need a websocket terminal session; both answer 501 NotImplemented.
- Container Instances: not supported and rejected with 400 InvalidRequestContent: Windows containers, gitRepo volumes, GPUs, liveness/readiness probes, init containers, zones, subnet and DNS configuration, diagnostics, confidential/dedicated SKUs, spot priority, encryption, extensions, UDP ports.
- Container Instances: azureFile volumes are copied from the Azure Files share when the containers start and written back when a container exits and when the group stops or is deleted, not synchronized live; the storage account key is accepted without being checked.
- Container Instances: the group address is 127.0.0.1 and ports are published on pool-assigned host ports (reported in a PortPublished event), not on the declared port numbers; Private addresses behave the same.
- Container Instances: restarting a failed container under Never is not done (the platform may restart it); the restart back-off starts at 10s and caps at 5 minutes. Resource requests are validated but only limits are enforced, and per-group CPU/memory maxima are not checked.
- Container Instances: sibling endpoints (locations/{loc}/usages, cachedImages, capabilities, the operations list, outboundNetworkDependenciesEndpoints, container group profiles) are not implemented; a restored snapshot brings groups back Stopped.
- Network: not modelled (they stay in the generic metadata-only store): load balancers, NAT gateways, application gateways, firewalls, VPN/ExpressRoute, private endpoints, application security groups, DDoS plans, service endpoint policies, flow logs, public IP prefixes, virtual network taps and every other Microsoft.Network type.
- Network: IPv6 private addresses on NICs are rejected; IPv6 public addresses come from 2001:db8::/32. Subnet addressing with ipamPoolPrefixAllocations and NAT/gateway-subnet rules are not enforced (NICs report the virtualMachine and primary back-references of an attached Compute VM but never hostedWorkloads).
- Network: GET operations/{id} is stateless (every id reports Succeeded); there are no failed or in-progress long-running operations. Error codes other than InUse*, PublicIPAddressCannotBeDeleted and InvalidResourceReference are not verified against Microsoft Learn (AddressSpaceOverlap, VnetAddressSpacesOverlap, SecurityRule*, PrivateIPAddress*, SubnetIsFull, InUseSubnetCannotBeUpdated, DnsRecordInUse).
- Network: PUT of a virtual network without a subnets (or securityRules, routes) key keeps the stored children; an explicit empty array removes them. ARM replaces the set on any PUT.
- Private DNS: auto-registration of NIC addresses into linked zones, one-registration-link-per-vnet and overlapping-namespace conflicts, zone deletion rules, $top paging of record sets by recordSetNameSuffix, and Microsoft.Network/dnszones (public DNS) are not implemented.
- Compute: not modelled (they stay in the generic metadata-only store): VM extensions and run commands, images and galleries, proximity placement groups, capacity reservations, dedicated hosts, disk encryption sets and disk accesses, restore points, SSH public key resources, usages and the operations list.
- Compute: virtual machines do not run; unmanaged (vhd) disks, inline networkInterfaceConfigurations, Spot eviction, boot diagnostics, maintenance, capture, reimage, reapply, runCommand, convertToManagedDisks, attachDetachDataDisks and simulateEviction answer 501 NotImplemented or are rejected. Platform images are not looked up (any publisher/offer/sku with a latest or Major.Minor.Build version is accepted and exactVersion is not reported); the vmSizes catalog is a representative subset available in every location and zone.
- Compute: disks accept Empty, FromImage, Copy and Upload; Import, ImportSecure, Restore and CopyStart are rejected, beginGetAccess/endGetAccess answer 501 (an Upload disk stays ReadyToUpload), and Ultra/Premium v2 IOPS limits, shared disks (maxShares), bursting, encryption sets and zone-versus-VM zone matching are stored but not enforced.
- Compute: scale sets are Uniform only (Flexible is rejected); instances are state records, so their network interfaces are not created in Microsoft.Network and subnets referenced by a scale set can still be deleted. Rolling upgrades, autoscale, scale-in policy, per-instance power actions and instance-level PUT/PATCH are not implemented.
- Compute: a virtual machine cannot be added to an availability set after creation (PropertyChangeNotAllowed) and an omitted availabilitySet, osProfile or storageProfile on update keeps the stored value. Network interfaces of a virtual machine in a removed resource group are released but a virtual machine whose NIC group is removed first keeps its dangling NIC reference.
- Identity: container group zones are still rejected; managed-identity role assignments and token endpoints (IMDS) do not exist, so a system-assigned principal has no permissions to evaluate.
- ManagedIdentity: listAssociatedResources, the identities/default scope and isolationScope are not implemented. Identity blocks (Compute, Web, Container Instances) resolve user-assigned identities by resource group and name, ignoring the subscription; deleting an identity that a resource still references is allowed and the reference then reports empty principalId/clientId.

### Deferred

- M7 initial implementation. No prior audit passes to report.
- M9 added the Microsoft.ServiceBus RP (ServiceBusNamespaceCRUD/ServiceBusQueueTopicSubscriptionCRUD/ServiceBusAuthorizationRuleListKeys). QC pass over the pre-existing implementation found and fixed two real bugs before any Terraform run (List not filtering by resource group for queues/topics/subscriptions; DeleteResourcesInGroup's cascade delete never matching due to a double-pipe key-prefix bug) -- see AZURE.md section 10.10's M9 entry for full detail.
- M9's first real-CI run (PR #2466, terraform-tests (6) job on Linux, past the macOS TLS-trust gap) surfaced a third real bug: classifyServiceBusPath had no case for namespaces/{ns}/networkRuleSets/default, which terraform-provider-azurerm's namespace Read calls unconditionally on every namespace regardless of SKU or config -- see ops.ServiceBusNamespaceNetworkRuleSet above and AZURE.md section 10.10's M9 entry for full detail. Checked queue/topic/subscription/authorizationRule Read functions in the same pinned source for the same class of unconditional sub-resource probe; none exists (each Read function only calls its own client.Get).
